Psychosis in an Adult: Rule Out a Cause, Then Time It

How long, and only during mood episodes?

Stem cuesDiagnosisManagementPractice
Bottom line

First rule out a drug or medical cause: urine toxicology, chemistry and TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone). Then time the psychosis against the gates: brief psychotic disorder 1 day to under 1 month, schizophreniform disorder 1 to under 6 months, schizophrenia 6 months or more. Psychosis only during mood episodes is a mood disorder with psychotic features.

How it hides in a stem
The clues that decided the two NBME questions
ClueWhat it points to
Delusion for 6 monthsToo long for brief psychotic disorder
Denies hearing voicesNo second symptom: not schizophrenia
No low or high mood; sleeps 6 to 8 hoursNo mood episode: not bipolar
Delusions and a voice, gone within a weekUnder 1 month: brief psychotic disorder
Six drinks the night it beganAlcohol rarely causes psychosis directly
Fired, walked out by securityA stressor, not a life-threatening event: not PTSD (posttraumatic stress disorder)
Diagnosis
Criterion A (schizophrenia) Symptoms – 2 or more of delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized or catatonic behavior, negative symptoms · Core – at least 1 is delusions, hallucinations or disorganized speech
Timeline gates
DisorderNeedsDurationMood episodes
Brief psychotic disorder1 or more core symptoms; full return to baseline1 day to under 1 monthNot only during them
Schizophreniform disorderCriterion A1 to under 6 monthsNone, or a minority of the illness
SchizophreniaCriterion A; functional decline6 months or more; 1 month activeNone, or a minority of the illness
Delusional disorderA delusion; Criterion A never met; otherwise functioning and behavior intact1 month or moreBrief, if any
Schizoaffective disorderCriterion A with a major mood episode; psychosis 2 weeks or more without oneOne illnessMost of the illness
Mood disorder with psychotic featuresPsychosis only in mood episodesThe episodeManic or major depressive
Substance-induced psychotic disorderDelusions or hallucinations tied to a drugDuring or soon after useNot a criterion
First tests
TestOrderResultWhat it tells you
Urine toxicologyFirstNegativeHelps exclude intoxication or withdrawal
Urine toxicologyFirstPositiveExposure, not cause: check the timing
Chemistry, glucose, TSHFirstNormalExcludes a metabolic or thyroid mimic
Brain MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)By branchLesionOnly with a neurologic finding
Management and treatment
Management ladder
TierInterventionEscalate when
First lineAntipsychotic; hospitalize if dangerous or unable to meet basic needsNo response after an adequate trial (4 to 6 weeks)
Second trialA different antipsychotic; long-acting injectable if nonadherent2 or more adequate trials fail, adherence confirmed
Treatment resistantClozapine, with ANC (absolute neutrophil count) monitoringTop rung
Practice
  1. 52-year-old man brought to the emergency department by police because of odd behavior, after an arrest for disturbing people living nearby; for 6 months he has been pushing flyers hard to promote a New Age healing business he runs from his home, and he claims special abilities that cure every kind of physical and mental illness; he is extremely upset about the arrest and is convinced that the police and the physician are plotting against him and his business; he insists he truly has special powers and could heal everyone in the waiting room; physical examination normal; mental status examination: denies any past psychiatric problems, depression, elevated mood or hearing voices; sleeps 6 to 8 hours a night; laboratory studies within the reference range → Delusional disorder → one delusion for 6 months with no hallucinations, disorganization, negative symptoms or mood episode
  2. 37-year-old man comes to the physician for strange experiences that began 2 weeks ago, right after his supervisor fired him when he had been expecting a promotion; a security guard watched him clear his desk and walked him out; he then had six drinks at a bar over 4 hours and felt that the other patrons knew about the firing and were watching and discussing him; the feeling was still there when he woke the next day; he drew his curtains and believed people on television were ridiculing him; during the following week he heard a man's voice saying he was a failure who would never amount to anything; he went out only to buy food and wore dark glasses so no one would recognize him; all of it was gone by the end of that week; no serious illness; takes no medications; drinks 2 to 3 beers each night; uses marijuana about once a month; physical examination normal; mental status examination: no hallucinations; thought process logical and goal directed; alert and oriented to person, place and time → Brief psychotic disorder → paranoid delusions and a voice after a stressor, gone within a week and well under 1 month
  3. 24-year-old man brought by his sister because for 3 months he has believed his neighbors implanted a tracking device in his tooth; he hears voices commenting on everything he does and has stopped attending classes; no episodes of depressed or elevated mood; vital signs within normal limits; urine toxicology negative; mental status examination: flat affect; oriented to person, place and time → Schizophreniform disorder → a delusion plus prominent voices for at least 1 month and under 6 months
  4. 26-year-old man brought by his parents; for 9 months he has heard voices and believed that television hosts send him coded messages; he lost his job, rarely speaks and has stopped bathing; no episodes of depressed or elevated mood; vital signs within normal limits; urine toxicology negative; mental status examination: flat affect, speech sparse → Schizophrenia → Criterion A symptoms with functional decline for 6 months or more
  5. 46-year-old woman brought by her employer's human resources officer because for 4 months she has written daily letters to a television news anchor she has never met, certain that he is in love with her; she works full time and runs her household without difficulty; no hallucinations; mood normal; sleeps 7 hours a night; vital signs within normal limits; laboratory studies within the reference range → Delusional disorder → an erotomanic delusion for at least 1 month, with functioning intact and no other psychotic or mood symptoms
  6. 34-year-old woman with 1 year of hearing voices that insult her and believing that her coworkers are plotting to poison her; the voices and the belief ran through two episodes during that year, each lasting more than 2 weeks, of depressed mood, loss of interest, poor sleep, excessive guilt and poor concentration nearly every day, which together covered most of the year; the voices and the belief have continued for 4 weeks since her mood returned to normal; vital signs within normal limits; urine toxicology negative; mental status examination: euthymic mood; full-range affect; hears insulting voices during the interview; alert and oriented to person, place and time → Schizoaffective disorder → Criterion A concurrent with major depressive episodes, 2 weeks or more of delusions and voices without a mood episode, and mood episodes for most of the illness
  7. 29-year-old man brought by his wife after 1 week of sleeping 2 hours a night, talking rapidly and spending their savings; he says God chose him to rule the world; 2 years ago he had a similar week, and his beliefs stopped when his mood settled; he has had no psychotic symptoms between episodes; vital signs within normal limits; urine toxicology negative; mental status examination: pressured speech; expansive affect; flight of ideas; alert and oriented to person, place and time → Bipolar disorder with psychotic features → the psychosis occurs only during the manic episode
  8. 22-year-old man with 2 days of believing that federal agents are following him; he has smoked methamphetamine every day for the past 3 days and has barely slept; no earlier psychiatric history; HR 96/min; BP 128/80 mm Hg; T 37.0 C; alert and oriented to person, place and time → Substance-induced psychotic disorder → the delusion began during stimulant intoxication; timing ties it to the drug
  9. 31-year-old woman with 5 days of believing that the government has hacked her phone and hearing whispers at night; no past psychiatric history; T 37.0 C; HR 88/min; alert and oriented to person, place and time; neurologic examination normal; serum chemistry panel and TSH normal → Urine toxicology screen → it helps exclude intoxication or withdrawal; imaging needs a neurologic finding or history
  10. 40-year-old man with 10 days of believing his coworkers are poisoning his food; yesterday he bought a knife to confront them; no past psychiatric history; vital signs within normal limits; urine toxicology negative; mental status examination: oriented to person, place and time → Hospitalization and an antipsychotic → likely harm to others: admit first, whatever the duration; involuntarily if he refuses and no less restrictive option is safe
  11. 33-year-old man treated for schizophrenia for 6 years still hears voices daily after adequate trials of risperidone and then olanzapine, with adherence confirmed by pill counts; vital signs within normal limits; mental status examination: flat affect; hears voices during the interview; no suicidal or homicidal ideation; alert and oriented to person, place and time → Clozapine → 2 or more failed adequate trials with documented adherence define treatment resistance
How NBME framed it: question 1 Every other symptom is cleared: no voices, no mood episode, normal sleep and labs. NBME says delusional disorder has no hallucinations; current criteria allow minor ones tied to the delusion.
Distractors: NBME question 1
Unchecked attributeSchizophrenia: needs a second Criterion A symptom; he has one delusion.
True-fact-wrong-slotBipolar disorder: no low or high mood, and normal sleep.
Unchecked attributeBrief psychotic disorder: under 1 month; his delusion has lasted 6.
Salient decoySchizoaffective disorder: no mood episode and no second Criterion A symptom.
How NBME framed it: question 2 A firing, a night of drinking and monthly cannabis put stressor and substance answers beside the psychoses; 1 week decides it.
Distractors: NBME question 2
Unchecked attributeDelusional disorder: needs 1 month or more.
Unchecked attributeSchizophreniform disorder: needs 1 to 6 months.
Salient decoySubstance-induced psychotic disorder: alcohol rarely causes psychosis directly; cannabis use is occasional.
True-fact-wrong-slotAdjustment disorder: psychotic symptoms would be atypical.
Salient decoyPTSD: losing a job is not a life-threatening event.
Pairs with Bipolar disorder: psychosis only during mania? Delirium: psychosis with a clouded, fluctuating sensorium?
Transferable rule

Rule out a cause, then ask how long the psychosis has lasted and whether it occurs only during mood episodes.
